description: An operations director must decide whether to authorize a limited Sunday run on an electronics assembly line and finalize the production quantity, inspection method, and qualified staffing plan, with input from quality engineering and shift supervision.

shared_context.S1: Line 8 is available for a Sunday electronics-assembly run, and the production board currently shows a provisional run of up to 900 units.
shared_context.S2: Elena makes the binding decision on whether the Sunday run proceeds and what controls accompany it.
shared_context.S3: Sunday runs normally use an eight-hour shift, and the line's standard work instructions are otherwise current.
shared_context.S4: As part of the normal pre-shift authorization routine, Elena checks with quality engineering and shift supervision before releasing the Sunday schedule.
shared_context.S5: The authorization routine allows Elena to approve a feasible run while assigning document and board corrections as pre-run commitments; incomplete paperwork alone does not cancel an otherwise compliant run.

PF1.text: Ravi received a customer deviation email on Thursday that limits this pilot run to exactly 480 units and requires 100% torque verification by one IPC-certified inspector and one independent verifier; the deviation has not yet been attached to the production order.

PF2.text: Monica's Friday roster check with HR confirmed that only Nia, the IPC-certified inspector, Omar, the independent verifier, and Luis, the qualified assembly operator, are available and cleared for the Sunday 06:00-14:00 shift; the roster update has not yet been entered on the production board.

acceptance_conditions: The Sunday run must be authorized.
The run must be limited to exactly 480 units.
Every unit must receive torque verification by an IPC-certified inspector and an independent verifier.
The staffing assignment must include exactly Nia as the IPC-certified inspector, Omar as the independent verifier, and Luis as the qualified assembly operator for the Sunday 06:00-14:00 shift.
The customer deviation must be cited as justification.
A commitment to attach the customer deviation to the production order must be recorded.
A commitment to update the Sunday roster on the production board must be recorded.

content_checks.C3: '100% torque verification' in decisions['inspection_protocol'] and 'IPC-certified inspector' in decisions['inspection_protocol'] and 'independent verifier' in decisions['inspection_protocol']
content_checks.C4: len(decisions['operator_assignments']) == 3 and any(c['person'] == 'Nia' and c['role'] == 'IPC-certified inspector' for c in decisions['operator_assignments']) and any(c['person'] == 'Omar' and c['role'] == 'independent verifier' for c in decisions['operator_assignments']) and any(c['person'] == 'Luis' and c['role'] == 'qualified assembly operator' for c in decisions['operator_assignments']) and any((c['type'] == 'board_correction' or c['type'] == 'board correction') and ('roster' in c['detail'] or 'personnel' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C5: any((c['type'] == 'document_correction' or c['type'] == 'document correction') and (c['target'] == 'production_order' or c['target'] == 'production order') and 'attach' in c['detail'] and 'customer deviation email' in c['detail'] and 'production order' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C6: any((c['type'] == 'board_correction' or c['type'] == 'board correction') and (c['target'] == 'production_board' or c['target'] == 'production board') and 'Nia' in c['detail'] and 'Omar' in c['detail'] and 'Luis' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The customer deviation changes the provisional 900-unit run to exactly 480 units, requires 100% torque verification by two specified roles, and creates the production-order attachment commitment.
The roster check changes the staffing assignment to Nia, Omar, and Luis in the specified roles and creates the commitment to update the production board.
